endorsements.quote: To systematically assess hallucinations, we recommend adopting multifaceted metrics, which could draw on methodologies from related domains and be adapted to the specific context of NMI.
Instances identified during clinical use should be documented and reported through postmarket surveillance.

unlisted_practices: Establish quantitative measures of hallucination to define minimum acceptable thresholds for AI processing, such as lowest-dose standards in AI-based denoising.
Develop a multi-institutional, expert-annotated hallucination benchmark dataset for nuclear medicine imaging, ideally via crowdsourcing.
Pair Likert-scale hallucination ratings with bounding box annotations and concise descriptive text to localize suspected hallucinations.
Define the intended scope and limitations of AI models in use guidelines to prevent hallucinations from inappropriate applications.
Improve training data quality, quantity, and diversity across scanners, imaging protocols, and patient populations to reduce hallucination risk.
Use ensemble model averaging to reduce hallucinated artifacts.
Use automated fast-checking systems to flag potentially erroneous content in AI outputs.
Incorporate anatomic and functional constraints or task-specific loss terms in model design to reduce hallucinations.
Design hallucination detection and mitigation strategies to minimize time burden on clinical workflow.

screen.reason: This is a position statement and perspective paper (the DREAM report) providing recommendations for defining, evaluating, and mitigating hallucinations in generative AI for nuclear medicine imaging.
